# Stabilization worker 001 — input action lifecycle

Actual worker: `/root/review001` under coordinator-owned `AUDIT-20261128`.
Reviewed baseline: `876ec252119d575a110f69c3f9b6140642a3f3c2`.
Scope: read-only inspection of `engine/input/include/ge/input/actions.hpp`,
`engine/input/src/actions.cpp`, relevant consumers, existing tests, and prior audit.
Only this requested ignored report was written. No source edits, compilation,
test execution, ledger mutation, staging, or commit.

## P2 — disconnecting any device restarts unrelated held actions

The queued `EventKind::Disconnected` branch in `Impl::apply_event` clears every
`BindingRuntime` (`engine/input/src/actions.cpp:733`), as does the direct
`InputSystem::disconnect_device` path (`engine/input/src/actions.cpp:1116`).
That discards `previous_down`, `held`, and `hold_fired` even for keyboard bindings
when an idle gamepad disappears.

On the next evaluation, the held keyboard still supplies a nonzero value, but
`evaluate_binding` sees `previous_down == false` and produces a new rising edge
(`engine/input/src/actions.cpp:909`). Immediate interaction publishes it as both
`pressed` and `triggered` (`engine/input/src/actions.cpp:924`). Hold interaction
loses its accumulated duration and can release an already-active hold, then
trigger again after another hold interval. Character control and prediction
consume `pressed("jump")` (`engine/physics/src/character.cpp:951` and
`engine/network/src/prediction.cpp:587`).

The existing worker-021 report in
`docs/production/integration-audit-register.json` already records an executed
direct/queued reproducer: after a held-key baseline, both paths publish
`down=1 pressed=1 triggered=1 held_seconds=0.1`; the expected next frame is
`down=1 pressed=0 triggered=0 held_seconds=0.3`. This review confirms that the
responsible code remains unchanged at the inspected baseline. I did not rerun
that historical reproducer.

**Minimal repair:** centralize device invalidation for direct and queued paths.
Retain runtime for bindings whose controls and chords do not reference the
removed device kind/full generation-bearing identity. Preserve continuity for a
wildcard binding when surviving devices still supply its active controls.
Cancel interactions that genuinely lose required input without synthesizing
Tap/DoubleTap completion. Simply deleting the global reset would otherwise
allow a disconnect to be interpreted as a normal tap release.

**Focused regression:** run both direct and queued disconnect variants while an
unrelated keyboard Immediate binding remains held; assert no additional
pressed/triggered edge and monotonic duration. Cover an already-fired Hold
without a release/retrigger, a wildcard gamepad binding supplied by a surviving
pad, and a disconnected Tap binding that must cancel without triggering.

## P2 — context consumption synthesizes a Tap release

This is a separate deterministic source trace, not a newly executed reproducer.

1. Define a low-priority `gameplay.tap` binding to Space with `Interaction::Tap`.
   Define a disabled higher-priority context with a distinct Immediate action,
   also on Space and with the default `consume=true`.
2. Press Space and update with `delta_seconds=0.1`. The low binding remembers
   `previous_down=true`, `held=0.1`; no tap has completed.
3. Enable the high-priority context and update again without any ButtonUp.

The high-priority binding consumes Space at
`engine/input/src/actions.cpp:1021`. `Impl::sample` skips that consumed control
at line 814, so the lower binding receives zero, without a release event. Its
remembered down state nevertheless creates `falling` and `completed_cycle`
at lines 910 and 911. Because the previous duration is below `tap_seconds`,
the Tap branch publishes `triggered=true` and `pressed=true` at lines 929 and
930. Opening the consuming UI therefore activates the lower gameplay action
while the key remains physically held. The same mechanism can finish an armed
DoubleTap when the second press is intercepted.

**Minimal repair:** distinguish a control hidden by consumption/suppression from
a physical neutral/release value. Cancel the hidden binding's interaction state
without Tap/DoubleTap completion. Preserve the normal aggregate release edge
for an Immediate/Hold action that was already down.

**Focused regression:** use the sequence above, assert that the low Tap remains
untriggered after context enablement, and confirm the physical button remains
down. Repeat with an armed DoubleTap and with an actual unconsumed ButtonUp
to ensure normal completion still works.

## Startup evidence and handoff

Read repository guidance, README, architecture/module boundaries, quality gates,
worker workflow, handoff, canonical task, public input contracts, existing input
integration tests, and prior worker-021 findings. The read-only startup commands
reported clean `main`, coordinator ownership, revision 527, current source
fingerprint, and current generated views. No task was claimed by this worker.
Coordinator retains source repair, regression execution, integration gates,
acceptance, and publication.

# Stabilization worker 002 — scene serialization review

Actor: `/root/review002`. Task: coordinator-owned `AUDIT-20261128`.
Baseline: `876ec25`. Scope: read-only review of
`engine/scene/src/serialization.cpp` and its public header, with supporting Scene
and binary-codec contracts. No source changes, builds, tests, ledger mutations,
commits, or additional delegation. This report is the only file written.

Startup observed clean `main`, ledger revision 527, coordinator ownership, and
current source fingerprint/generated views. Read the repository, architecture,
quality/workflow, handoff, and applicable public contracts. Read worker 019's
pertinent prior report in the integration audit register. The three queued
findings remain present in the reviewed baseline.

## 1. P2 — validation accepts documents outside encoded size limits

**Anchors:** `serialization.cpp:105` (`validate_document`), `:475`
(`validate_scene_document`), `:571` (`import_scene_document`); actual bounded
serialization starts at `:218` (`encode_document`).

The validator checks aggregate text, counts, extension payload sizes, and semantic
fields. It never charges the encoded manifest or node section, nor the complete
archive/table overhead. A default one-node document with
`max_section_bytes = 32` passes public validation, while its nodes section needs
114 bytes and encoding fails with `DocumentError::Limit`. The public import path
uses the same weaker validator and can therefore import a document that exceeds
its supplied archive limits.

**Bounded fix:** use shared overflow-safe encoded-size accounting during
validation. With the present format, the manifest is `24 + name bytes + sum(8 +
key bytes + value bytes)`. The nodes section is `4 + sum(110 + node-name bytes +
optional 48-byte bounds + sum(4 + tag bytes))`. Every extension section is
`4 + payload bytes`; the outer envelope is 32 bytes, inner header 40 bytes,
table entries 32 bytes each, and inner CRC 4 bytes. Check each section and the
complete archive before allocating serialized output. This preserves the
existing caller-visible limit contract without weakening validation semantics.

**Regression:** exercise exactly-at-limit and one-byte-over-limit manifest,
nodes, extension, and total archive sizes; require agreement among validation,
encoding, store replacement, and import. Failed encoding must retain destination
bytes; rejected replacement must retain document/epoch; rejected import must
leave existing scene entities unchanged.

## 2. P3 — accepted limits make a newly constructed store unsavable

**Anchors:** `serialization.cpp:66` (`check_limits`), `:921`
(`SceneDocumentStore` constructor).

`check_limits` accepts `max_archive_bytes` of 165–167. An empty document needs
168 bytes: 32 envelope + 40 inner header + 64 table + 24 manifest + 4 node count
+ 4 CRC. The constructor uses the incomplete validator, so construction succeeds
but the initial `encode()` fails.

**Bounded fix:** derive the minimum from shared format constants and require at
least 168 bytes. Shared size validation from finding 1 should also validate the
initial document. Correct the stale `minimum_node_bytes = 107` at `:349` to 110
using the same format definitions; current scalar readers still reject truncated
records, so this constant is an early-admission issue rather than successful
malformed publication.

**Regression:** reject capacities 165, 166, and 167; accept and round-trip the
empty store at 168. Verify the node count preflight against a truncated fixed
node record.

## 3. P2 — diff inspection misses a real parent change

**Anchor:** `serialization.cpp:640`, `diff_scene_documents` movement predicate.

Before: node IDs `[1,2,3]`, with ID 3's parent index 0 (ID 1). After: IDs
`[2,1,3]`, with ID 3 still at index 2 and parent index 0 (now ID 2). The child
payload is identical, and the movement predicate compares only its own ordinal
and numeric parent index. Consequently the summary contains no change for the
reparented ID 3. The complete replacement bytes remain correct.

**Bounded fix:** compare the referenced parents' persistent identities as well
as the existing conservative ordinal checks, with a distinct root representation
and ordinal fallback for anonymous parents.

**Regression:** require a `Moved` entry for ID 3 in this fixture and its reversed
patch; also cover unchanged persistent parent after reorder, anonymous parents,
and root-to-child transitions. Patch application/reversal must still reproduce
the respective canonical archives.

## Preservation review and evidence limits

Source inspection found staged decode publication, private candidate edits,
epoch conflict rejection, and required-extension import gating intact. The
import wrapper reserves its returned node mapping before live scene mutation.
No additional last-good-state defect is asserted. Workflow `status`, `next`,
and `check` were observed; `check` passed. No engine verification was executed
by this worker; prior worker 019's reproducer evidence remains historical.

Coordinator next action: assign the bounded repairs and meaningful regression
coverage, then run the relevant integration gate on a coordinated source freeze.

# Stabilization worker 003 — assets streaming and catalog

Actual worker: `/root/review003`. Baseline: `876ec25`. Read-only audit of the asset catalog/cache and streaming implementation, public headers, and runtime consumers. Reviewed repository instructions, architecture, workflow, handoff, ledger, and prior integration reports. Startup observed clean `main`, ledger revision 527, coordinator-owned `AUDIT-20261128`, and current source/views. No builds, tests, engine execution, source edits, ledger changes, commits, or child agents. This report is the only written file.

## P2 — revision reconciliation can permanently miss dependency-graph changes

**Evidence:** `engine/assets/src/streaming.cpp:306–318,354–359,445–457,880–887,994–999`.

Closures are rebuilt only when `catalog_dirty` is set. Nevertheless, every `reconcile()` reads current catalog records and immediately advances `Node::revision`, even when closures have not been refreshed. `poll_catalog_changes()` subsequently marks a tracked asset dirty only if an event revision differs from that already-updated node revision. Both notifications emitted by `AssetCatalog::update()` carry the new revision (`catalog.cpp:811–825`), so both can be ignored.

**Deterministic public-API sequence:** request A whose dependency is B; consume existing catalog history; change A's definition to depend on existing C; call `reprioritize(ticket, same_priority)` before the next pump. That call reconciles A's revision but leaves the request closure A/B. Later pumps consume A's matching invalidated/updated events without rebuilding the closure. `dependencies_ready()` cannot find C in `nodes`, so A remains `waiting_dependencies`, while obsolete B remains demanded. A sufficiently long unrelated change backlog causes the same ordering without an intervening API call. This requires no resource-pressure or worker race.

**Repair:** keep graph revision/change tracking separate from node import revision, or rebuild affected closures whenever reconciliation observes a revision change. Consuming a delayed notification must not treat an unprocessed definition change as processed.

**Regression:** with ample capacities, exercise the sequence above and a `changes_per_poll=1` backlog variant. A must eventually publish using C without manual retry; B must lose current demand. Also retain an explicit old-version pin to verify historical dependency ownership survives.

## P2 — closure replacement becomes unrecoverable at the tracked-asset limit

**Evidence:** `streaming.cpp:263–278,281–318,327–340,891–905`.

`set_closure()` checks `nodes.size() + additions` before releasing obsolete closure members. On failure it preserves the old closure; reconciliation still counts those old members as demanded even though the request has an error. `prune_nodes()` therefore cannot reclaim them. `retry()` repeats the same rejection indefinitely.

**Minimal sequence:** configure `max_assets=2`, `max_jobs=1`; request A→B; update A to depend on C; call `retry(ticket)` to force closure reconciliation. The desired closure A/C contains two assets, but the existing A/B nodes plus C are counted as three. This fails even before any job is launched and continues failing on repeated retries. Releasing/recreating the request works, demonstrating that the final demand fits.

**Repair:** stage the replacement demand graph and budget its resulting tracked-node union, retaining only nodes still required by other requests or active retirement. Historical pinned versions already have their own ownership graph and should not force obsolete demand nodes to remain.

**Regression:** replace A→B with A→C at capacity and prove eventual readiness without releasing A's request. Include shared B demand and an active B job so legitimate live ownership remains charged.

## Existing integration gap

The prior audit's missing resource adapters remains unresolved: the only catalog `register_type()` caller installs binary, and runtime `ResourceCache`/`AssetStreamer` consumers are catalog commands and scene partition orchestration. No mesh/image/audio importer or publication adapter was found. This is an already-recorded limitation, not a newly counted defect. No additional definite late-result publication or cancellation-lifetime defect was established in the reviewed paths.

# Stabilization worker 006 — AssetStreamer closure reconciliation

Actual worker: `/root/review006`. Subordinate exclusive scope under coordinator-owned `AUDIT-20261128`. Reviewed repository instructions, architecture/module boundaries, streaming/catalog headers and implementation, test conventions, and worker 003's findings. Read-only startup saw ledger revision 528 with concurrent source drift, as expected; no ledger/view repairs attempted.

## Changes

- `engine/assets/src/streaming.cpp`: revision observation now leaves `catalog_dirty` pending even if an API reconciliation updates the node before its catalog event arrives. A delayed event matching the node revision can no longer erase the need to refresh dependency closures.
- Replaced per-request reload admission with staged replacement closures. Their resulting tracked-asset union is budgeted together with all active import nodes, allowing obsolete shared demand to disappear atomically at `max_assets` without deleting required demand from another request.
- Failed capacity admission remains pending for reconciliation. A live obsolete import retains its tracking slot and all existing byte reservations until the normal completion/retirement path releases them; a later reconciliation then admits the replacement automatically.
- Retained/pinned `Version` dependency ownership is unchanged and remains independent of obsolete demand nodes.
- `engine/assets/include/ge/assets/streaming.hpp`: clarified tracking capacity and closure refresh/retry ownership.
- `tests/asset_streaming_audit_tests.cpp`: four deterministic cases using memory files, a single worker, explicit executor waits, and a paused pending job. No sleeps or timing races.

## Regression expectations

1. Load A→B, pin its historical version, drain history, update A→C, and reprioritize before the update events are polled. A reaches the new revision, C becomes ready, tracked demand contains only A/C, and the old A pin still owns B until released.
2. With `changes_per_poll=1`, unrelated events ahead of A's update do not strand A on its obsolete closure.
3. Two consumers sharing A→B can both transition to A→C at `max_assets=2` before any import starts, using their original request tickets.
4. A separate B consumer keeps B's pending import live when A changes to C. Releasing that consumer cancels B but preserves its tracking/byte/cache reservations until retirement. A then reaches ready automatically with no repeated retry or request recreation.

## Executed evidence

Strict isolated GCC 14 compilation passed for the test and both old/new streaming translation units using C++20, pthread, and `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wshadow -Werror`.

Artifacts in `out/stabilization/006/`: `streaming_before.cpp` captured from HEAD, three object files, and `audit_before` / `audit_after`. - `out/stabilization/006/audit_after`: **passed, 4/4 cases, 90 checks**.
- `git diff --check`: passed after the implementation edit.

No full build, shared build-output mutation, shared CMake edit, ledger mutation, commit, publication, child agent, or `catalog.cpp` change.

# Worker 007 — WorldPartition correctness review

## Finding

No definite defect established in the assigned partition implementation. No source or test changes made.

Reviewed `engine/scene/src/partition.cpp` and its public header against Scene, StreamingPolicy, AssetStreamer, PhysicsWorld, and CollisionWorld contracts and implementations, plus the runtime architecture and current integration tests.

- Activation waits for every required readiness bit at the current producer coordinate epoch. Producer startup precedes preparation so thrown/rejected preparation and activation retain a retirement cleanup obligation.
- Retirement gates borrowed roots without destroying them, preserves descendant enable flags, waits for producer cleanup, releases pins, invalidates/destroys its stream consumer, and acknowledges the reservation only after required streamer job drainage.
- Root bindings reject duplicate/cross-region ownership and require live top-level Scene entities. Active/loading records detect destroyed/reparented roots.
- Origin shifting validates root matrices and physics caches before mutation, restores saved roots on an explicit physics rejection, and blocks subsequent coordinate work after ambiguous exceptions. Nested body shifts use cached pre-shift poses. Shift history gives independent reader cursors.
- Immutable policy request epochs remain admission labels; producer readiness and shifted acknowledgements separately track the current epoch. Rewriting request tokens would violate StreamingPolicy's contract.

## Evidence and limitations

Read-only audit only; no build or runtime test executed, as builds are coordinator-owned. Existing runtime tests cover module installation but contain no direct partition lifecycle regression. A malformed Scene transform is not itself forbidden by the partition's logic-only readiness contract, so the gate's treatment of Scene invalid-node counts was not changed speculatively.

Startup workflow commands observed revision 528 and the expected stale source fingerprint during concurrent worker edits. No ledger, CMake, or unrelated files changed. Coordinator can record this no-change review without additional integration work.

# Worker 008 — Collision geometry/query audit

## Scope and finding

Reviewed `collision.hpp` / `collision.cpp`, math primitive consumers, dynamic-tree query reporting, and integration callers. Shape validation, transform admission, plane half-spaces, query truncation/filtering, and generation-checked collider access/removal were inspected. This module has no ray or sweep API; those implementations are outside the assigned files.

Two reproduced narrowphase false negatives shared a units error: squared segment lengths were compared against the linear `tiny` tolerance. A valid capsule with a 5e-7 m centerline was collapsed to its first endpoint during capsule/capsule testing. A short diagonal capsule beside a box edge skipped its interior closest-point minimum during capsule/box testing.

## Changes

- `engine/physics/src/collision.cpp`: use `tiny * tiny` for squared-length degeneracy/minimization checks, with a units comment.
- `tests/collision_audit_tests.cpp`: three compact regressions covering endpoint capsule contacts, interior capsule/box edge contacts, and exactly collapsed centerlines. Each nondegenerate scenario checks both ordinary and small scale.
- Public API unchanged.

## Evidence and integration

Isolated current-source compilation used the dev strict warning flags plus `-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections`; only collision.cpp, math.cpp, and this test were compiled. Unused runtime registration was discarded, avoiding the known stale Kernel archive ABI. No full build or build-tree writes were performed.

- Before fix: 1/3 cases passed; both targeted contact regressions failed.
- After fix: 3/3 cases, 24 checks passed; compile exit 0.
- `git diff --check -- engine/physics/src/collision.cpp tests/collision_audit_tests.cpp`: passed.
- Logs: `out/stabilization/008/{build-before,run-before,build-after,run-after}.log`.
- Coordinator: add `ge_add_runtime_test(collision_audit collision_audit_tests.cpp)` and include it in fresh central builds.

## Limitations / dependency note

No full runtime, ray/sweep, or exhaustive primitive-pair validation was attempted. Startup agent-state source drift was expected from concurrent owner edits; ledger/generated views were untouched.

A separate math-owner review candidate remains: collision accepts triangle cross magnitudes above 1e-12, while math `closest_point(Triangle)` treats magnitudes at or below 1e-10 as degenerate. For triangle (0,0,0), (2e-6,0,0), (0,2e-6,0), a sphere at (5e-7,5e-7,0), radius 1e-7, lies on the face but the math fallback considers only its edges. This discrepancy was source-inspected, not executed or changed here; resolving the shared math contract belongs to its owner.

# Worker 010 — terminal kernel lifecycle and CLI shutdown review

Assignment `/root/review010`, subordinate to coordinator-owned `AUDIT-20261128`.
Read worker brief, AGENTS, README, architecture/runtime composition, quality gates,
workflow, handoff and existing runtime consumers. Read-only startup observed ledger
revision 528 and expected concurrent source staleness. No ledger/CMake/build-tree,
staging, commit or publication changes.

## Findings and repairs

- Confirmed that system-triggered shutdown previously tore down services while the
  current frame continued invoking later systems. Direct commands, queued work and
  several registration/schedule APIs also remained usable after terminal shutdown.
- Added a latched shutdown request and active-command depth, using existing tick
  and drain guards. Shutdown immediately rejects new dispatch/queued admission,
  module/system/command/shutdown registration and schedule/enabled-state edits.
  Teardown waits for all active tick/drain/command callbacks to unwind, including
  nested commands and exception paths. The remaining systems and unexecuted
  command batch/queue are discarded. Drain results cover invoked commands only.
- A shutdown-interrupted tick returns false. A started frame keeps its tick/time
  and system statistics but performs no frame-event retirement. Shutdown during
  pre-frame command processing admits no frame. `request_stop()` keeps its existing
  finish-current-frame behavior and leaves commands/registration available.

### Minimal repair / integration dependency

Expose a stable, unique per-lifetime identity from `geometry::MeshLibrary` and
store/check it in mesh cache keys and pruning. Handle generation, revision,
library address, or source mesh address alone cannot establish a new lifetime.
This requires the geometry owner plus the batching owner. A local safety
mitigation is clearing retained mesh preparation between builds, at the cost of
cross-build reuse. No repair was made because this assignment is read-only during
the integration freeze.
